item.title: Nadi, Suva aim to strengthen positions in Round 11 of Skipper Cup and Marama Championship
item.description: In the Skipper Cup this Friday, Navosa will host Suva at Lawaqa Park at 2pm, with the two teams’ U20 sides meeting at 10am. Malolo will face Naitasiri at 4pm, with their U20 match scheduled for 12pm.
item.content:encoded:
In the Skipper Cup this Friday, Navosa will host Suva at Lawaqa Park at 2pm, with the two teams’ U20 sides meeting at 10am.

Malolo will face Naitasiri at 4pm, with their U20 match scheduled for 12pm.

At King Charles Park in Nadi, the hosts will take on Rewa at 3pm, while the U20 sides will meet at 1pm.

On Saturday, Tailevu will travel to Taveuni to face the home side at Wairiki Grounds at 3pm, with the U20 match scheduled for 1pm.

Nadroga will meet Kadavu at Lawaqa Park at 3pm, with their U20 sides playing at 1pm.

Ba will host Lautoka at 4R Electric Govind Park at 3pm, while their U20 sides will meet at 11am.

Meanwhile, the Subrails Marama Championship will also feature a busy weekend of fixtures.

On Friday, Rewa will face Nadi at King Charles Park at 11am, while Macuata will host Tailevu at Subrail Park at 1pm.

On Saturday, Namosi will take on Naitasiri at the Uprising Grounds in Pacific Harbour at 11am, followed by the match between Nasinu and Suva at 1pm at the same venue.

Nadroga will then face Kadavu at Lawaqa Park at 11am, while Ba will take on Lautoka at Govind Park at 1pm.

item.title: Fiji Bati set to name new captain for Rugby League World Cup next week
item.description: Head coach Mick Potter, who guided the Bati to the semi-finals at the 2017 Rugby League World Cup, says the captain will be named as the team begins preparations at the Uprising Resort in Deuba. With both Kamikamica and Kikau unavailable, veteran Wests Tigers captain and three-time premiership winner Apisai Koroisau is among the likely candidates to lead the side.
item.content:encoded:
Head coach Mick Potter, who guided the Bati to the semi-finals at the 2017 Rugby League World Cup, says the captain will be named as the team begins preparations at the Uprising Resort in Deuba.

With both Kamikamica and Kikau unavailable, veteran Wests Tigers captain and three-time premiership winner Apisai Koroisau is among the likely candidates to lead the side.

Potter is also expected to select a leadership group, with the focus on ensuring the squad works together to produce results.

He says the expectation is for every player to give their best individually and collectively.

The Bati have reached the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals in 2008, 2013 and 2017, losing to Australia on each occasion.

item.title: Wasasala’s 90th-minute winner lifts Labasa to 2-1 victory over Suva
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Mansi Chand · 07/10/2026 Christopher Wasasala struck in the 90th minute to secure a dramatic 2–1 victory for Labasa over Suva in the FMF Inter-District Championship at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Mansi Chand · 07/10/2026

Christopher Wasasala struck in the 90th minute to secure a dramatic 2–1 victory for Labasa over Suva in the FMF Inter-District Championship at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Labasa took the lead in the 22nd minute before Suva responded five minutes later, with Andrew Naicker finding the equaliser in the 27th minute.

The teams went into halftime locked at 1-all.

Both sides created opportunities in the second half, but neither could find the decisive goal as the match appeared destined to end in a draw.

However, Labasa continued to push forward and were rewarded in the dying moments when Wasasala found the back of the net in the 90th minute.

The late goal sparked celebrations from the Labasa camp and sealed three valuable points for the side.

Suva pushed for an equaliser in stoppage time, but Labasa held firm to secure the 2–1 win.

The victory gives Labasa an important boost ahead of their match against Rewa today.

Labasa coach Jerry Sam says he is pleased with his team’s performance.

Sam says his instructions to the players were clear, to control the game and score early.

Sam is also calling on Labasa fans to turn up in numbers today.

In other matches of Day 1, defending champions Stratum/Lincoln Rewa thrashed Nasinu 5-0, Vantex Solution Navua defeated Pacific Heavy Industries Nadi 3-0, while Dayal’s Steel Ba edged Khelvin Realtors Lautoka 2-1.

The results mean Rewa and Labasa have three points each in Group A while Navua and Ba have three points each in Group B.

In today’s matches, Nadi will play Lautoka at 1.30pm, Suva will face Nasinu at 3.30pm, Ba will play Navua at 5.30pm, while Labasa will face Rewa at 7.30pm.
